standard.title: Locate, organise and respond to information in texts
standard.description: locate, organise and respond to key information related to familiar content in spoken, written and multimodal texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate key information in familiar texts and respond with opinions and retelling using modelled language (AC9LCH2C03). They can identify main points and make personal connections. They have not yet gathered, organised and re-presented information from multiple sources, nor conducted interviews or produced structured summaries or responses for an audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate, organise and respond to key information in familiar spoken, written and multimodal texts — including gathering from multiple sources, organising findings, retelling and summarising, and presenting information in different forms for purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Locating and identifying information in texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can locate familiar words and key information in a range of text types and identify the purpose, main content and key features of the text.
nodes.minimum_width: Locate at least three key pieces of information in a familiar text and identify the text's main purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Locate familiar characters, words or information in spoken, written and multimodal texts; identify main purpose and meaning; discuss key features of different text types (stories, informative texts, songs, packaging, educational programs); notice how First Nations Australian languages change according to relationships.
wider: Compare how the same information is presented in two different text types or formats — identify what is the same and what is different about how meaning is conveyed
Investigate a real-world text (packaging, sign, advertisement) in the target language — identify all the information it contains and explain how the visual and written elements work together
nodes.hinge_reason: Locating and identifying information is the prerequisite for all text response and re-presentation. Students who cannot extract key information from texts cannot organise, summarise or present it in a different form — the core demand of this descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Information location strategies transfer across text types — stories, songs, packaging, educational media, informative texts. Practising with varied text types builds flexible comprehension strategies that work beyond a single familiar format.

success_criteria: Locates at least three key pieces of information from a familiar text
Identifies the main purpose of the text and at least one key feature of its format

nodes.label: Gathering and organising information from multiple sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can gather information from more than one source and organise it to present findings in a different form.
nodes.minimum_width: Gather information from at least two sources and organise findings into a different format — for example, a timeline, graph, table, or summary list.
nodes.typical_width: Gather information from a range of sources — interviews, texts, surveys, media — and organise findings in a new format; create timelines, picture graphs, annotated displays or summaries; interview family or peers to collect information about cultural practices, languages or experiences.
wider: Compare findings gathered from different sources — identify where sources agree, differ, or complement each other, and discuss why
Design and conduct a class survey, analyse the results, and present findings in an annotated target language graph or display

response_modes.reason: Gathering from multiple sources and re-presenting requires students to hold information across sources and decide how to organise it. Scaffolded organisational tools — templates, graphic organisers, guided interview questions — support this cognitive work before students can manage it independently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Interviews with family members about language history, cultural practices and migration experiences are a uniquely powerful data source for background language learners. Width investment in interview-based information gathering activates authentic cultural knowledge and produces genuinely meaningful responses.
success_criteria: Gathers information from at least two sources
Organises and presents the information in a different form — timeline, graph, table, or summary

nodes.label: Retelling, summarising and performing in response to texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can retell or summarise the main information or ideas in a familiar text, and create a performance or presentation in response.
nodes.minimum_width: Retell or summarise the main points of a familiar text using at least four target language sentences, and create at least one text or performance in response.
nodes.typical_width: Retell and summarise spoken and written texts — stories, folk tales, reports — with attention to main information, sequence and key ideas; read aloud or recite texts with attention to pronunciation and intonation; create performances or presentations in response to texts.
wider: Create an alternative version of a familiar text — changing the ending, updating the setting, or retelling from a different character's perspective
Perform a cultural legend or folk tale for a specific audience, selecting language and presentation approach appropriate to that audience

response_modes.reason: Retelling, summarising and performing integrates information location (node 1) and multi-source organisation (node 2) into a full communicative response. The teaching investment is in creating genuine performance or presentation conditions — real audiences, real purposes — that require students to select, organise and communicate effectively.

success_criteria: Retells or summarises main points of a familiar text using at least four target language sentences
Creates a performance or presentation in response to a text, demonstrating understanding of content
